title: FizzBuzz
description:
Return a list of strings counting from 1 to n. Replace multiples of 3 with "Fizz", multiples of 5 with "Buzz", and multiples of both with "FizzBuzz". Every other number becomes a string.

Keep the function name fizzbuzz. Return the list rather than printing it. For n less than 1, return an empty list.

title: Reverse a string
description:
Write reverse_string(text) that returns the characters of text in reverse order. Preserve spaces, punctuation, and capitalization. An empty string should return an empty string.

Try solving it with a loop or a slice. Return a new string; do not print it.

title: Find the largest number
description:
Write largest_number(numbers) that returns the largest value in a non-empty list of integers. The list may contain only negative numbers.

Do not use the built-in max function for your first attempt. Track a candidate as you visit each number. You do not need to handle an empty list.

title: Count vowels in a word
description:
Write count_vowels(word) that returns the number of English vowels in a string. Count a, e, i, o, and u in both uppercase and lowercase. Treat y as a consonant.

Spaces and punctuation should not be counted. Return an integer, not a printed message.

title: Is it prime?
description:
Write is_prime(n) that returns True when an integer is prime and False otherwise. A prime is greater than 1 and has exactly two positive divisors: 1 and itself.

Pay special attention to 0, 1, 2, and negative numbers. Return a Boolean. A loop up to the square root of n is enough, but a simpler correct loop is welcome.
expectedOutput:
is_prime(7) → True
is_prime(1) → False
is_prime(2) → True

title: Sum the even numbers
description:
Write sum_even(numbers) that returns the sum of all even integers in a list. Odd numbers should be ignored. Zero is even.

An empty list, or a list with no even numbers, should return 0. Negative even numbers count too. Return the sum rather than printing it.

title: Find the first duplicate
description:
Write first_duplicate(numbers) that scans a list from left to right and returns the first value that has already appeared. If there are no duplicates, return None.

For [3, 1, 2, 1, 3], the answer is 1, because the second 1 appears before the second 3. Try using a set to remember values you have seen.

title: Student grade calculator
description:
Write calculate_grade(score) that converts a score from 0 to 100 into a letter grade: A for 90–100, B for 80–89, C for 70–79, D for 60–69, and F below 60.

Boundary scores belong to the higher grade. All inputs will be numbers between 0 and 100. Return a single uppercase letter.
